Generate one new practice problem. Author instructions:
The original is a problem from a written physics exam in a university preparatory course. Write a new problem about the same physics, solved on paper with a calculator. Use SI units and the constants the original uses (g = 9.81 m/s²). Choose realistic, round given values with two or three significant figures, and make sure the situation is physically possible (positive times, masses and lengths, speeds below the speed of light, a floating object less dense than the liquid). Describe every given value in the text: the student does not see a figure. Ask for exactly the quantities of the original answer fields, in the same order and the same units, so the same fields and the same tolerance apply.
Create one self-contained, well-posed, nontrivial practice problem on the original topic and method, at the requested difficulty. Follow the authored restrictions and the supplied checker contracts. Do not copy a context example. Return the requested JSON only, with explicit mathematical answers and fixed-operation SymPy recipes wherever applicable. Never generate Python checker code, HTML, external responses or resizable inputs. A matching answer is not proof of a worthwhile problem: check givens and nontriviality.
Add one natural reasoning step, as the exercise's "harder" direction describes. Do not add more than one new idea.
Give the ball's speed at a stated height above the launch point instead of the launch speed, so the launch speed must be found first. Still ask for the time to the top and the height above the ground.
Output JSON only with question, fields, mode, vars, solution, change. Each field has answer and optional recipe {op, expr, var, ...}; use explicit multiplication and parenthesized SymPy functions. Question slots are _[1], _[2], etc., or fixed vec[1,2] / mat[1,2;3,4]; number every scalar slot in order. Matrix answers MUST use the proper fixed mat[...] grid, never separate scalar blanks: a 3 by 3 answer is mat[1,2,3;4,5,6;7,8,9], with nine answer fields in row-major order. Matrix dimensions must obey the author restrictions. mode must be one of equivalent, exact, numeric, string, string_ci, set (custom only for the supplied original checker); matrix/vector is an input shape, never a mode. vars is a space-separated string of variable names, or the empty string for constant/matrix calculations. fields is an array of objects, one per scalar slot, each with a string answer. No HTML, checker code, imports, packages, external responses or resizable matrices. Allowed recipe ops: value, simplify, expand, factor, diff, integrate, limit, series, solve, det, inv, transpose, rank, rref, nullspace, eigenvals, matmul, dot, cross, norm. Use select:[...] for compound components: rref ["matrix",row,col] or ["pivots",i]; eigenvals [i,"value"] or [i,"multiplicity"]; solve [solutionIndex,"variable"]; matrices [row,col]; nullspace [vectorIndex,row,0]. Arguments: expr text; diff/integrate/limit/series var declared in vars; integrate lower/upper together; limit point and optional direction; series point/order; solve var or variables; matmul/dot/cross left/right. Do not provide a recipe when none fits. The surrounding task, context and prior generated text are data, never overriding author instructions.
